sources.title: GCC library-recognized built-ins
sources.version_or_date: GCC 4.8.2 manual; release dated 2013-10-16 by GCC release history.
sources.sections_read: Section 6.55 opening paragraphs and library built-in list.
sources.confirmed: GCC recognizes ordinary C library function names and corresponding __builtin_ names; when a case is not optimized it emits a library call.
sources.limits: Applies to library-equivalent operations; instruction-only primitives need callable implementations, and no unoptimized-build instruction-count guarantee was verified. Explicit same-type/same-address wording was confirmed only in the date-unknown current manual. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C15.json.

sources.title: OCaml manifest external declarations
sources.sections_read: Title page; section 19.1.1 located through find results.
sources.confirmed: The manual identifies itself as OCaml 4.01 dated 2013-09-12; section 19.1.1 states that manifest external declarations let clients call the C primitive directly instead of through an OCaml function.
sources.limits: OCaml's FFI, object representation, and closure conventions differ; function-value uses may still need adapters, and Rust debug-build performance was not measured. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C15.json.

sources.title: GHC generated PrimopWrappers
sources.sections_read: Id type definitions; Note [Primop wrappers] reached using find.
sources.confirmed: GHC 7.6.3 represents primitive operations using PrimOpId metadata and has automatically generated curried GHC.PrimopWrappers bindings; the note explicitly says routing unsaturated native uses to those bindings would require additional work.
sources.limits: The verified GHC 7.6.3 source documents GHCi use and identifies native unsaturated-application routing as additional work; it centralizes wrappers rather than proving their runtime cost disappears. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C15.json.

sources.title: OCaml manifest external declarations
sources.sections_read: Section 19.1.1, PDF pages 274–275, external declarations and public interfaces.
sources.confirmed: External declarations bind typed OCaml function values, support currying, and can be exposed either as regular values or as manifest externals; manifest externals enable direct primitive calls.
sources.limits: OCaml's FFI, object representation, and closure conventions differ; function-value uses may still need adapters, and Rust debug-build performance was not measured. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C15.json.

sources.title: GHC generated PrimopWrappers
sources.sections_read: Id.lhs hasNoBinding and Note [Primop wrappers], lines around 332–366.
sources.confirmed: The generated GHC.PrimopWrappers functions are used by GHCi; the note identifies a possible additional conversion for unsaturated native primitive applications, rather than claiming that conversion already exists.
sources.limits: The verified GHC 7.6.3 source documents GHCi use and identifies native unsaturated-application routing as additional work; it centralizes wrappers rather than proving their runtime cost disappears. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C15.json.

sources.title: Go math/bits compiler-recognized ordinary functions
sources.version_or_date: Go 1.9 release notes; release dated 2017-08-24 by official announcement.
sources.sections_read: Introduction and New bit manipulation package section, with section reached via find.
sources.confirmed: Go 1.9 introduced math/bits as ordinary library functions with optimized implementations, additionally recognized as intrinsics on most architectures.
sources.limits: Later evidence after the cutoff; intrinsic support depends on architecture and release, and optimization-disabled behavior was not verified. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C15.json.

sources.title: Common Lisp compiler macros
sources.version_or_date: Live Common Lisp HyperSpec page; copyright 1996–2005, exact publication date unverified.
sources.confirmed: A function name can simultaneously name an ordinary function and a compiler macro; the expansion mechanism can replace a call form while preserving the function binding.
sources.limits: Expansion is discretionary and can decline, so guaranteeing wrapper-free direct calls in unoptimized builds requires a compiler policy beyond the portable mechanism. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C15.json.

sources.title: m_define.htm
sources.version_or_date: Live Common Lisp HyperSpec page; copyright 1996–2005, exact publication date unverified.
sources.confirmed: The standard mechanism registers a separate compiler expansion for a function name, can handle direct and explicit funcall forms, and may decline expansion by returning the original form.
sources.limits: This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C15.json.
